svg.title: How long an effort can be held
svg.desc: Line chart of the longest-held effort the engine accepts, as a share of VO2 reserve, for averaging windows of 6, 15 and 30 minutes, 1 hour and 3 hours. The limit is the athlete's lactate-threshold share plus a margin that narrows from 0.25 at 6 minutes through 0.18, 0.13 and 0.09 to 0.05 at 3 hours, and never goes above 1.05. For a recreational athlete, threshold 0.75, that is 1.00 for 6 minutes, 0.93 for 15, 0.88 for half an hour, 0.84 for an hour and 0.80 for three hours. At 3 hours a beginner is allowed 0.75, a trained athlete 0.88 and an elite one 0.93; trained and elite limits are cut to 1.05 at the shortest windows.
